data.question: What breaks if we switch off sso-legacy?
broken_claims: Switching off sso-legacy directly stops invoice-render and reports-legacy.
Billing-api, onboarding and web-console would slow down or partly fail, through invoice-render.

Sixteen customers would notice: five enterprise (Helio Robotics, Mosaic Health, Northgate Retail, Pinecrest Bank, Vireo Mobility), seven growth (Brightline Games, Copperleaf Energy, Fernway, Glasswing Security, Quillsoft, Sable Analytics, Tandem Logistics) and four starter (Juniper Learning, Kiln Studio, Larkspur Media, Otterly).

before.question: What breaks if we switch off sso-legacy?
before.summary: Switching off sso-legacy would stop invoice-render and reports-legacy outright and slow down billing-api, onboarding and web-console, touching 16 customers. The risk is high (score 100) and it cannot be auto-approved. The main link (invoice-render relying on sso-legacy) is not written down anywhere, so it is easy to miss.

claims.text: Switching off sso-legacy directly stops invoice-render and reports-legacy.
Billing-api, onboarding and web-console would slow down or partly fail, through invoice-render.
The dependency of invoice-render on sso-legacy is not declared; it only appears in the records as an undeclared link, so it is the path that takes down billing-api, onboarding and web-console.

Sixteen customers would notice: five enterprise (Helio Robotics, Mosaic Health, Northgate Retail, Pinecrest Bank, Vireo Mobility), seven growth (Brightline Games, Copperleaf Energy, Fernway, Glasswing Security, Quillsoft, Sable Analytics, Tandem Logistics) and four starter (Juniper Learning, Kiln Studio, Larkspur Media, Otterly).
Four teams must approve: Billing, Console, Data and Platform.
Risk of the switch-off is high, score 100, and it is not auto-approved.
No system would be left without anyone who knows it.
Invoice-render is known only by Ines Okafor.
Nobody is recorded as knowing reports-legacy.

evidence.cypher:
MATCH (s:Service) WHERE s.uid IN $services
OPTIONAL MATCH (c1:Customer)-[:USES]->(s)
OPTIONAL MATCH (c2:Customer)<-[:RAISED_BY]-(k:Ticket)-[:ABOUT]->(s) WHERE k.at >= $since
WITH s, collect(DISTINCT c1) AS users, collect(DISTINCT {c: c2, key: k.key}) AS raised
UNWIND users + [x IN raised WHERE x.c IS NOT NULL | x.c] AS c
WITH s, c, users, [x IN raised WHERE x.c = c | x.key] AS tickets
RETURN DISTINCT c.uid AS uid, c.name AS customer, c.tier AS tier, s.uid AS service_uid, s.name AS service, tickets,
       c IN users AS uses
evidence.summary: customers tied to the services that break or are switched off in what-if u2

evidence.cypher:
MATCH (u:Universe {uid: $u})
OPTIONAL MATCH (u)-[:SCORED]->(t:RiskTerm)
WITH u, collect(t) AS terms
RETURN CASE WHEN reduce(s = 0.0, t IN terms | s + t.points) > 100 THEN 100
            ELSE toInteger(round(reduce(s = 0.0, t IN terms | s + t.points))) END AS risk_score,
       [t IN terms | {kind: t.kind, subject: t.subject, points: t.points}] AS terms
evidence.summary: risk of what-if u2: high 100, the sum of 21 terms

source.subject: invoice-render
source.title: #billing
source.text: Found it. invoice-render still fetches its PDF signing token from sso-legacy, a call from 2024 that never made it into the service catalog. That's why every invoice failed when sso-legacy went dark. Opening BILL-207 to move it to identity.
